topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Genetic basis and multifactorial nature of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core biological concepts of cancer as a disease of accumulated mutations evolving in microenvironments alongside the interplay of bad luck and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Epidemiological patterns and geographic variation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines international epidemiological data to highlight how cancer incidence varies geographically and implicates environmental and genetic factors.

topics.label: Pathogenic drivers of cancer and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, focusing in detail on the discovery and mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma driven by Epstein-Barr virus and malaria.

topics.label: Dietary, environmental, and chemical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific environmental and chemical mutagens—such as aflatoxins, UV radiation, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, and aromatic amines—and the biological mechanisms through which they damage DNA.

topics.label: Tumor promoters, host factors, and mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, developmental cell host contexts, and resulting mutational signatures influence carcinogenesis, concluding with a comprehensive midpoint summary.

topics.label: Methodologies for determining carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe and evaluate the epidemiological, animal in vivo, and Ames in vitro experimental methodologies used to identify and prove carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenesis around individual and societal risk-benefit decisions and summarising key takeaways.
